author: maintainer-agent

patch.value:
## Scope, from the live audit
Four legacy codes on terminal items only: ninety-eight retired no-active-blocker sentinel references; eight duplicated relationship spellings between terminal endpoints; eight terminal-only ordering cycles spanning forty-nine items, the largest across twenty-three closed milestone items; three dangling references to absent targets.

## Why this needs to be a batch and not opportunistic cleanup
Touching a closed item updates its timestamp, and the changelog buckets by that timestamp — so ad hoc repair silently drags years-old closed work into the current release notes. Doing all of it at once, deliberately, with the changelog effect measured and regenerated as the final step, is the only safe shape.

## Method
Read-only classification first, producing the full edge list per code. Then a single mutation batch. Then changelog regeneration and an explicit statement of which buckets moved and why. Never mutate a closed item outside this batch.

## Boundary
Removal of meaningless edges only. This wave adds no new relationships — enrichment is the separate active and terminal backfill waves.
Graph wave: changelog-safe legacy edge hygiene batch — retire the no-active-blocker sentinel, duplicate spellings, terminal ordering cycles, and dangling terminal references

The no-active-blocker sentinel references are removed from all holders; blocker state derives from real edges only; Duplicated parent and child spellings between terminal endpoints collapse to the canonical single spelling; Terminal-only ordering cycles are broken by dropping the single lowest-evidence edge per cycle, with the choice recorded; Dangling terminal references to absent items are resolved or removed with the rationale recorded on the holder; The changelog effect is measured before and after; regeneration runs as the last step and any bucket movement is stated explicitly in the batch record; pm graph audit reports zero findings for all four legacy codes after the batch
The audit reports zero legacy findings without dragging closed items into a release changelog

One hundred and fifty-eight terminal items carry edges that mean nothing: a retired sentinel, duplicated parent and child spellings of the same relationship, ordering cycles between closed milestones, and references to items that never existed. Every graph traversal and every audit run pays to skip them.
Removes the permanent noise floor from graph governance so that a non-zero audit finding count becomes actionable again instead of expected.
The audit's four legacy codes report zero, executed as one deliberate batch whose changelog effect is controlled and stated up front.
The audit itself names the remediation as a dedicated changelog-safe closed-item batch and explicitly forbids ad hoc repair. That batch has never been scheduled, so the findings recur on every run.
